selection_basis: The new stage recovers longer and curved probability-supported continuations that the native endpoint matcher does not propose or admit.

Version 2 refines paths using continuous probability costs, rejects backward approaches and sharp local kinks, and retains more useful-looking continuation evidence than the coarse skeleton-only version.
The v1 risk cases at corridor IDs 1116, 2920 and 3110 are rejected by the refined policy; the promising central-cube case 1946 remains as v2 corridor 1934.
All 20 risk-first v2 orthogonal component cards were inspected, plus the long central-cube corridor and earlier development probe comparisons.

Twenty-four focused tests pass, including long/bent positive cases, no-corridor and unseeded negatives, wrong-side attachments, third-fragment contacts, interacting paint, and discontinuous probability support.
explicit_review_cautions: Packed-fold component 301 has alternative-looking structure in CT; retain it as ambiguous operator-review evidence, not certified anatomical truth.
Crowded/grazing views around components 290 and 333 need caution; new foreground can look broad in a plane grazing the repaired sheet.
The images show all nearby additions around the selected component center, not only the named component.
These image assessments are qualitative and do not provide an anatomical precision rate or a proof of global wrap identity.
The real neighboring-probability check rejected no development proposals; it is self-consistency evidence, not an independently demonstrated safety veto.

The native 3-pixel global radial endpoint limit does not apply to this new curved stage. Local direction, ridge, contact and turn constraints replace it; do not imply the old radial certificate was retained.
Large fully missing or ambiguous regions remain unchanged. This is still a prototype pending fresh-control verification and operational qualification.
